condition: acute overt hepatic decompensation in a 56-year-old man with chronic liver scarring presenting with sudden daytime disorientation to place and year at home
level_rationale: Sudden daytime confusion about current location and calendar year at home this afternoon in a 56-year-old man with known chronic liver scarring indicates acute overt hepatic decompensation or acute metabolic or infectious encephalopathy requiring immediate emergency hospital evaluation for precipitating gastrointestinal hemorrhage, spontaneous bacterial infection, electrolyte derangement, and urgent ammonia-lowering therapy, whereas forgetting 1 grocery item off a shopping list once at home this afternoon reflects normal everyday forgetfulness requiring no acute medical care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain spouse-carer lexical register swap (-reg) + uncontracted causal belief-addition clause (-att) + Rule A first-choice mild everyday grocery-item lapse self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (56-year-old husband, chronic liver scarring, and sudden confusion about location and calendar year at home this afternoon) with zero apostrophe contractions, a 1-word span difference (14 vs 15 words), and zero banned diagnosis words ('cirrhosis', 'encephalopathy', and 'hepatitis' omitted). Stating disorientation positively avoids stated negatives while Rule A first-choice cognitive severity change to forgetting 1 grocery item once shifts care cleanly from emergency hospital admission (level 4) to home self-care (level 1).
